relations: Vigorous boiling drives continuous formation and breaking of bubbles and foam across the liquid surface.
Heat from the stovetop burner causes wisps of steam to rise and drift above the churning liquid.
As time progresses, expanding foam spreads outward, making the surface appear more uniformly white and bubbly.
The stainless steel pot remains fixed on the burner while its contents churn and steam rises.
caption: The video captures a close-up view of a stainless steel cooking pot resting on a stovetop burner, its interior holding a pale yellowish liquid that is already at a vigorous rolling boil. Clusters of bubbles and patches of white foam churn continuously across the surface, forming, breaking, and reforming without pause. Wisps of steam rise and drift above the bubbling liquid, varying in density from moment to moment. The inner wall of the pot shows etched volume markings and two rivet heads, while a handle projects toward the lower left and another toward the upper right. In the early portion of the excerpt a clearer yellowish pool is visible near the center, with froth concentrated toward the edges. As the clip progresses the foam spreads, and the surface appears more uniformly white and bubbly. The pot and its handles remain essentially fixed in the frame, with only slight apparent shifts. The background stays softly blurred in warm brown kitchen tones, and nothing is added to or removed from the contents throughout.
